mem.7:
May 8, 2023 — Caroline and Melanie (“Mel”) caught up. Mel was busy with work and children. Caroline had attended an LGBTQ support group the day before; hearing trans people’s stories made her feel accepted, supported, and more courageous about embracing herself. She planned to continue her education and explore counseling/mental-health careers to help people with similar experiences. Mel said she’d make a good counselor. Caroline shared a photo of a dog walking past a wall painted with a woman; Mel liked the painting. Mel shared her 2022 painting of a sunrise over a lake, which she valued for self-expression, creativity, and relaxation. Caroline praised the colors. Caroline left to research; Mel went swimming with her kids.

May 25, 2023 — Mel said she had run a mental-health charity race on May 20. It made her reflect on well-being and self-care; she was trying to make daily time for running, reading, or violin, though self-care remained a work in progress. Her kids were excited for summer; family was considering camping in June. Caroline was researching adoption agencies. Having a family and giving children in need a loving home had long been her dream. She shared a photo of an adoption-agency sign/building. She chose the agency because it supports LGBTQ+ adopters and felt hopeful, though she had much to learn. She looked forward to creating a family, while aware single parenting would be challenging. Mel said she’d be an awesome mom; Caroline hoped to offer a safe, loving home, and Mel felt she would provide love and stability.

June 9, 2023 — Caroline described speaking at a school event the previous week about her transgender journey and encouraging student involvement in the LGBTQ community. She felt powerful sharing struggles, coming out, and personal growth; audience members related and were inspired to be better allies. She said conversations about gender identity and inclusion promote understanding, acceptance, and hope. Caroline began transitioning around 2020. Mel praised her courage and advocacy. Caroline called friends, family, and mentors her “rocks”; she had known her support-network friends for four years, since moving from her home country around 2019. Their support was especially important after a difficult breakup. Caroline shared a family/friends photo in a yard. Mel said her husband and children motivate and support her; she and her husband had been married five years (since around 2018). She shared a photo of a man and little girl in front of a waterfall and a wedding photo of herself in a dress holding a bouquet. Caroline congratulated her. Mel also shared a family picnic photo (man and woman sitting on a blanket eating); she treasured the games, food, and time together, which made her feel alive and happy. Caroline agreed that time with loved ones brings gratitude and happiness; family is everything.

June 27, 2023 — Caroline shared a photo of a necklace with a cross and heart, a childhood gift from her grandmother in Sweden. It represents love, faith, and strength, and reminds her of her roots and family’s support. Mel shared patterned bowls and asked about treasured objects. Caroline’s friend had made her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday, ten years earlier (around 2013); its design and colors remind her of art and self-expression. Mel said she had taken her family camping in the mountains the previous week (around June 20): nature walks, hiking, campfire marshmallows, and an amazing summit view. Her two younger children love nature; she treasured the trip. Caroline was glad they made memories.

Caroline remained interested in counseling/mental-health work, possibly supporting trans people’s self-acceptance and mental health. She shared a bookshelf photo and described attending an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on Friday, June 23, about therapeutic approaches and working effectively with trans people. It was enlightening; professionals’ dedication to safe spaces inspired her. Counseling and support groups had helped her own journey and motivated her to create a welcoming place for others. Mel encouraged her and also shared a photo of a bookshelf in a room.

July 3, 2023 — Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade the previous week. Its joyful atmosphere made her feel she belonged and showed how much the community had grown. It motivated her to use her story to help others; she remained excited about counseling/mental-health work. Mel had signed up for a pottery class the day before; she found pottery therapeutic, creative, and expressive. She shared a photo of someone holding a frisbee and one of a bowl she made, decorated with a black-and-white flower. She was proud of it and said pottery was important in her life, helping her express emotions and bringing joy. Caroline praised her creativity and said she was learning piano. Caroline planned to attend a transgender conference in July to meet people and learn about advocacy; Mel wished her fun and safety.

July 6, 2023 — Caroline had been looking further into counseling/mental-health work; helping people and making a positive impact felt challenging but rewarding. Mel said she took her kids to a museum on July 5 and shared a photo of two children playing in a water-play area. They especially enjoyed the dinosaur exhibit, learning about animals, and seeing bones; it reminded Mel why she loves being a mom. Caroline said motherhood was awesome and she was building a library for her future children, with children’s classics, stories from different cultures, and educational books. She shared a bookcase photo and looked forward to reading with them. Mel’s favorite childhood book was *Charlotte’s Web*; friendship and compassion meant a lot to her. She shared a photo of a cover showing a girl and cat. Caroline said those themes made her appreciate friends and family who helped her through transition. Caroline had picnicked with friends the previous week and shared a photo of women sitting on a blanket in a park. Her support network gave love, guidance, and acceptance throughout her transition; their unconditional encouragement helped her accept and grow into her true self, and she couldn’t have done it without them. Mel also shared a photo of her family camping at a beach campfire; they love it and feel closer together.

July 12, 2023 — Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ conference on July 10. Meeting people with similar journeys in a welcoming environment made her feel accepted and grateful for the community. It reinforced the importance of fighting for trans rights and spreading awareness. She noted progress but said more was needed and wanted to help. She was still looking into counseling and mental-health jobs so people would have someone to talk to. Her own mental-health struggles and helpful support had motivated her to help others on similar journeys. Mel praised her and shared a photo of a book cover with a gold coin; a book she read the previous year reminded her to pursue dreams. Caroline said books guide and motivate her and help her discover herself. Her favorite was *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family; it made Caroline feel connected and hopeful. She shared a photo of a dog in a boat on the water. The book taught her self-acceptance, finding support, and that hard times don’t last; hope and love exist. They agreed pets bring joy and comfort. Mel shared photos of two little girls on steps with a dog and a cat lying on the floor. Her family has a dog and cat named Luna and Oliver; they are sweet, playful, and brighten the house. Mel also shared pink sneakers (Caroline called the color purple); they were running shoes. Mel had been running farther since the prior chat to destress and clear her mind, improving her mental health, and planned to continue. She had shared photos of the shoes being worn and in a box. Caroline encouraged her and emphasized self-care and mental health.
mem.13:
Caroline (surname unknown) and Melanie (surname unknown) are friends/supporters who appreciate each other. Caroline says Melanie helps her remember happy moments; Melanie says Caroline makes struggles more bearable. They attended a Pride festival together in 2022. On 17 Aug 2023 they agreed to plan a summer outing, possibly catching up and exploring nature.

CAROLINE
- Transgender; had been transitioning for three years as of 9 Jun 2023. Sweden is her home country. She moved away from it four years before 9 Jun 2023; friends she has known since then supported her through her transition and difficult breakup. Friends, family, and mentors are major sources of support. Their love, guidance, and acceptance helped her accept and grow into herself.
- LGBTQ support group on 7 May 2023 felt accepting and inspiring and gave her courage to embrace herself. She has struggled with mental health; counseling and support groups helped her and inspired interest in helping others.
- Exploring counseling/mental-health work, especially supporting trans people, since at least May 2023. Attended an LGBTQ counseling workshop on 23 Jun 2023 and found it enlightening. Wants to provide a safe, welcoming place and help people accept themselves. Attended a school talk the week before 9 Jun about her journey and LGBTQ involvement; students’ encouraging reactions inspired allyship. She wants to promote understanding and acceptance.
- Attended an LGBTQ pride parade in late June/early July 2023 and an LGBTQ conference on 10 Jul; felt welcomed, belonging, and motivated to support trans rights and raise awareness. Joined a pride parade on 11 Aug, describing it as energetic and loving. Joined a parade with her transgender teen mentee in June; seeing the teen encouraged by acceptance was a highlight. She joined an LGBTQ youth mentorship program around 15–16 Jul and works with a trans teen on confidence and positive strategies.
- Joined Connected LGBTQ Activists on 18 Jul 2023. The group meets, plans campaigns/events, supports members, and gives a platform for LGBTQ rights. Missed her city’s parade on 15–16 Jul but felt its message reminded people they are not alone.
- Pursuing adoption as a single parent, to give children a safe, loving home. Longstanding dream; researching agencies by 25 May, particularly an LGBTQ-inclusive agency. Grateful for friends/mentors and hopeful but aware of the work ahead. Attended an adoption council meeting on 14 Jul. Applied to agencies during the week before 23 Aug; excited and nervous, with help from an adoption advice group.
- Building a library for future children: classic children’s books, multicultural stories, educational books; looks forward to reading to them. Loves reading. Favorite book: *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, an inspiring true story about a trans girl and family; helped her feel connected and hopeful, taught self-acceptance, seeking support, and that hard times pass. On 12 Jul a book-cover photo Melanie shared reminded Caroline not to give up. Favorite childhood book not specified.
- Art is therapeutic and helps her explore transition, changing body, identity, and imperfections; she paints to tell her story, promote inclusion/diversity, and help people understand trans experiences. Painting “Embracing Identity” depicts a woman’s journey to acceptance, comfort, and love; intended warmth and self-acceptance. Made a blue-faced woman self-portrait around 14–20 Aug 2023; felt liberated and empowered. Planned an LGBTQ art show for Aug 2023; painted a tree and bright sun inspired by an LGBTQ center, symbolizing unity/strength. Supports LGBTQ rights and wants to live authentically and help others do so.
- On 17 Aug 2023, upset by religious conservatives’ comments during a hike; it reminded her of ongoing LGBTQ-rights work, but supportive people reassured her.
- Attended an LGBTQ youth conference planned for Jul 2023. Favorite color blue; it relaxes her. Learned piano by 3 Jul. Has guinea pig Oscar, who especially likes parsley.
- Childhood horseback riding with her father through fields was special; has always loved horses. Necklace with cross and heart was a gift from grandmother in Sweden when young; represents love, faith, strength, roots, family support. Friend made her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday, about 2013; colors/pattern evoke art and self-expression.
- Caroline says family time brings happiness and gratitude; “family is everything.” Photo described as family posing in a yard does not establish all pictured are relatives.

MELANIE
- Has husband and children; married about 2018 (five years married as of 9 Jun 2023; exact date unknown). Husband and children motivate her. Family helped during a move with practical help and love. Family camping, hiking, and exploring forests/mountains connect them and create happy memories.
- Busy with work and children on 8 May 2023. Children excited for summer; discussed June camping. Camping trips include nature, hikes, campfires, marshmallows and stories. Took family camping in mountains during week before 27 Jun 2023; younger children love nature, view from summit was amazing. Family camped 1–2 Jul 2023; she enjoyed unplugging. Family likes beach camping; usually visits beach once or twice a year, and she recently went with children, happiest seeing them enjoy it. In 2022 watched Perseid meteor shower camping, made wishes under clear starry sky; awe-inspiring. Meaningful memory: youngest daughter’s first steps. Family brings her joy and love.
- Ran mental-health charity race on 20 May 2023; found it rewarding and thought-provoking. Self-care is a work in progress; says caring for herself helps her care for family. Daily running, reading, or violin refreshes her. By 12 Jul, running farther/longer helped stress and mental health. Creativity and family bring peace.
- Painting helps her express feelings, create, and relax. Painted a lake sunrise in 2022. On weekend 8–9 Jul 2023, painted a sunset/palm tree with children; they enjoy nature-inspired painting. Finished another similar painting by 17 Jul. Pottery is a major part of her life, therapeutic, calming and joyful. Signed up for class 2 Jul; made a black-and-white flower bowl and felt proud. On 17 Aug showed a colorful bowl made to catch the eye and make people smile. Calls art a sanctuary, comfort, learning, happiness, and fulfillment. Painted a horse on a wooden wall; animal painting feels peaceful. Took children to pottery workshop 14 Jul; they made clay sculptures, including a dog-face cup.
- Took children swimming (8 May 2023), to a dinosaur museum (5 Jul; they loved bones, animals, and learning), and to a Matt Patterson concert for daughter’s birthday (13 Aug; praised his voice and songs). Favorite childhood book *Charlotte’s Web*, for friendship and compassion.
- Flowers represent joy, growth, beauty, and appreciating small moments; wedding flowers remind her of the day. Wedding was loving and joyful with loved ones; best part was marrying her partner and promising forever. Cherishes family time and feels alive and happy with loved ones.
- Dog and cat named Luna and Oliver; which name belongs to which is unspecified. Also pets Bailey and Oliver mentioned later; Oliver hid a bone in her slipper. Photo showed black dog lying in grass with frisbee; identities of people/pets in other shared photos are not always established. Melanie once fed a carrot to a horse. On 9 Jun said courage for her family is motivated by their love.
- Shared a photo of a man and little girl at a waterfall; people are not explicitly identified. Also shared wedding-bride photo and photo of man/woman eating on a blanket; described family outing with games, good food, and time together. 
- Painted lake sunrise in 2022; art helps express feelings and unwind. On 17 Aug 2023 Caroline and Melanie reaffirmed mutual friendship and support.
mem.19:
Caroline (surname unknown) is a transgender woman; Melanie (surname unknown) is her friend and mutual supporter. They appreciate and encourage each other. Caroline moved from an unspecified home country about 2019; friends she had known four years by June 2023 supported her, especially after a difficult breakup. Family, friends, and mentors helped Caroline through transition and self-acceptance. Some friends did not accept her transition; her current relationships feel more genuine. Melanie says her husband and children motivate her; family is her greatest source of love and support.

Caroline attended an LGBTQ support group on May 7, 2023, and found trans stories inspiring and the group accepting; this gave her courage to embrace herself. She had been transitioning for three years by June 9. She advocates for LGBTQ inclusion: gave a school talk about her journey in the week before June 9, encouraging students to participate and be allies; their reactions were encouraging. She wants to use her voice to support trans people and promote understanding. She attended an LGBTQ counseling workshop June 23 and a pride parade during June 26–July 2, feeling welcomed and inspired. Attended an LGBTQ conference July 10 and a council adoption meeting July 14. Joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth July 15–16 and mentors a trans teen, helping build confidence; they attended a June pride event where Caroline was moved by the teen’s joy and community support. Joined Connected LGBTQ Activists July 18; group meets, plans campaigns/events, and supports members. Missed her city’s July 15–16 parade. Volunteered at an LGBTQ youth center by Aug 28, shared her story, found it emotional and fulfilling, and planned to continue; group prepared a children’s talent show for September. Attended a trans poetry reading Oct 6, finding it safe and empowering.

Caroline’s own experience of mental-health struggles and the support she received motivates interest in counseling/mental-health work, especially supporting trans people. She wants to offer a safe, welcoming space. She planned to attend a trans conference in July. Art has helped her explore gender, accept herself, and express hard-to-say feelings; she has made art since about age 17. Her painting about being a trans woman uses red/blue for binary gender and blended colors to reject rigid categories. Other works include “Embracing Identity” (acceptance, warmth, self-love), a tree and sun inspired by an LGBTQ center (unity/strength), stained glass about growth, potential, and togetherness, and a self-portrait with blue face (liberating, therapeutic). She enjoys flowers and nature subjects, abstract art, guitar (since about 2018), and piano; “Brave” by Sara Bareilles is meaningful. She planned an LGBTQ art show for August, later September, featuring LGBTQ artists to promote acceptance. A religious-conservative group upset her during a hike; supportive people reassured her. She enjoys blue, which calms her.

Caroline has long wanted to adopt and provide children a safe, loving home. By May 25, 2023, she was researching inclusive LGBTQ adoption agencies and intended to parent alone, hopeful but aware it would be hard. She sought friends’/mentors’ support. Applied to agencies the week before Aug 23 and was excited/nervous; got help from an adoption advice group. On Oct 13 contacted her mentor and felt ready. Passed agency interviews by Oct 20, a major step. Hopes to adopt children who have lacked a home and give them love, acceptance, and support. Advised Melanie Oct 13 to research agencies/lawyers and prepare references, finances, medical checks, and emotionally for a long wait.

Caroline’s grandmother in Sweden gave her a cross-and-heart necklace when she was young; it represents faith, love, roots, strength, and family. A friend made her a painted bowl for her 18th birthday, about 2013. Has guinea pig Oscar, especially fond of parsley. Rode horses with her father as a child. Enjoys reading; favorite book is *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, which helped with hope, self-acceptance, and finding support. She is making a future children’s library with classics, multicultural stories, and educational books. Favorite childhood book unknown; Melanie’s is *Charlotte’s Web*.

Melanie is married (five years by June 2023, wedding circa 2018) and has children, including a youngest daughter and a son. Family outings and camping are especially meaningful. She enjoys beach trips (usually once or twice yearly), mountains, forest hikes, campfires, marshmallows, stories, and nature; family camped July 1–2, 2023, and in the mountains the week before June 27. In 2022 they watched the Perseids and made wishes. She remembers her youngest daughter’s first steps. Took children swimming (May 8), to a dinosaur museum (July 5), park (Aug 27), pottery workshop (July 14), and beach. Children enjoy nature and painting together; painted a palm-tree sunset July 8–9. On Aug 24 she volunteered with family at a homeless shelter, finding it hard but worthwhile. On Aug 13 celebrated her daughter’s birthday at a Matt Patterson concert. In October road trip, family visited Grand Canyon; son had an accident but was okay, frightening family and reminding Melanie to cherish them. Children were scared but reassured; she says they are resilient and give her strength. Trail outing Oct 19 helped her relax. Oct 21 bought two wooden doll figurines symbolizing family love.

Melanie values daily self-care: running, reading, clarinet (learned young), violin, and creativity; says caring for herself helps her family. Running farther by July 12 improved her mental health. She enjoys painting and pottery, about seven years by Sept 2023; pottery is therapeutic, expressive, calming, and important to her. Signed up for pottery July 2; made black-and-white flower bowl, colorful bowl, floral plate (Aug 24), and other work. September injury forced pottery break; by Oct 13 she was reading Caroline’s recommended book and painting. Paintings include lake sunrise (2022), horse on wooden wall, sunflower, pink-sky sunset, and abstract blue work; blue calms her. She likes landscape/still life and flowers, which recall joy and her wedding decor. Family loves painting together. Melanie plays clarinet and likes Bach, Mozart, and Ed Sheeran’s “Perfect.” Enjoys live music; saw band Summer Sounds playing upbeat pop. Pets include dog and cat Luna and Oliver (which name matches which unspecified); also mentioned Bailey and Oliver. Oliver hid a bone in her slipper; fed a carrot to a horse. Melanie shared a photo of black dog with frisbee. Melanie once shared photos of family scenes; pictured people are not necessarily identified. Caroline and Melanie attended a Pride festival together in 2022; planned a summer 2023 outing but completion unspecified.
